claims.explanation: AM-251 is a CB1/ CB2 receptor antagonist that blocks endocannabinoid signaling; selectivity likely reflects dependence on CB1 receptor (CNR1) expression and downstream MAPK/PI3K signaling, with sensitive lines enriched for RAS/RAF pathway activation (KRAS, BRAF, NF1) and PIK3CA mutations that may create addiction to endocannabinoid-driven survival signals. Lines with intact PTEN or without these drivers tend to be less affected, suggesting that oncogenic MAPK/PI3K activation plus CNR1 expression predicts sensitivity.

features.basis: AM-251 is a CB1 antagonist; CB1 expression is required for its pharmacologic effect (PMID 10698714, 19887554)
BRAF-mutant melanoma and other lines are enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with MAPK-driven survival
KRAS-mutant lines (gastric, pancreatic, colorectal) are enriched among sensitive lines
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and appears in several sensitive lines
PIK3CA mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines, suggesting PI3K pathway dependence
PTEN-mutant lines are more frequent among least-affected lines, suggesting intact PTEN may not be required for resistance but PTEN loss alone is insufficient
EGFR-mutant lung lines appear in both sensitive and resistant groups, but some sensitive lines carry EGFR mutations
TP53 mutations are ubiquitous and not discriminating; listed as a weak negative correlate
AM-251 also targets GPR55, which can promote proliferation; expression may mediate sensitivity
AM-251 targets GPR18; expression could contribute to selective effects
MAP2K1-mutant lung line is among sensitive lines, supporting MAPK pathway dependence
ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines, possibly linking chromatin remodeling to drug response
